transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Rachel Kim (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Dr. Anika Patel (Luminar Head of MLOps), Jared Thompson (Luminar Infra), Sasha Ortiz (Luminar Procurement)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Rachel opened with renewal timeline; customer requested 20% uplift in reserved capacity plus EU region onboarding and VPC/private link. SE walked through VPC options and KMS integration. Procurement asked about billing amendment and PO timeline. Agreed to run a 1-week benchmark and exchange security docs.

Topics: renewal timing, capacity uplift sizing, EU region onramp, VPC networking and KMS/HSM, SOC2/ISMS requests, pricing tiers, pilot benchmarking.

Transcript:
00:00 Rachel Kim: okay hi everyone uh thanks for joining. we know Sasha's on the call for procurement, hey.
00:07 Dr. Anika Patel: yeah thanks Rachel, appreciate it. we wanted to make sure we lock timeline before EOY, so that capacity's ready in january.
00:14 Rachel Kim: totally. quick agenda - confirm renewal terms, talk uplift numbers, vpc onboarding plan, security checklist, next steps. Marcus i'll hand to you for the vpc bits after the context.
00:25 Marcus Lee: cool, hey everyone. i'll try to keep it high level, then drill if needed.
00:30 Jared Thompson: cool. just to set context, current committed capacity is 1.5m token units / month across us-west and us-east. our new pipeline will push up to 2.1m for january and we want eu-west active for some percent of traffic by february.
00:48 Rachel Kim: okay that's helpful. when you say 2.1m token units is that a sustained baseline, or peak?
00:55 Jared Thompson: that's baseline expected, peak to 3.3m during business hours. so we need predictability for daytime qps.
01:03 Marcus Lee: noted. the good news is Dedicated reserved pools can be sized to match baseline and you can buy burst capacity. for latency-sensitive routes we recommend pinning a model variant and using our low-latency SKU.
01:17 Dr. Anika Patel: question on hosted vs dedicated - cost tension is real. we don't want to manage infra but costs are higher on hosted. what are the tradeoffs here?
01:27 Rachel Kim: yep so classic latency vs cost. hosted api gives you no infra ops and simpler rollback; dedicated adds predictability and data isolation. with Redwood Optimize we can recommend batching/kv-cache settings to move cost down which helps if you go hosted.
01:41 Jared Thompson: when you say kv-cache are you referring to prefix caching or something else? last time our team saw K-V cache was tricky with streaming.
01:49 Marcus Lee: yeah good callout. we support prefix/KV caching and continuous batching; streaming with KV is a special path — sometimes the transcript (laugh) — the runtime will fall back to the streaming-optimized kernel, but you lose some cache-hit benefits. we'll show this in the benchmark.
02:10 Sasha Ortiz: this is procurement - just flagging we need a contract amendment template, and we need to see a draft with pricing for the uplift and the eu region add-on. also payment terms, net30 preferred.
02:21 Rachel Kim: got it. i'll attach a pricing worksheet and amendment example. quick clarifying Q: do you want the EU region to be private (VPC) or are you okay if it's hosted in our eu region?
02:33 Dr. Anika Patel: for a start, hosted eu is fine, but we need to plan for a VPC/on-prem timeline in case regulatory audits push us. so step one hosted, step two vpc private.
02:43 Marcus Lee: that aligns with a progressive rollout — can stage eu-hosted for jan then start VPC onboarding in feb, with a target of completing by end of march. VPC path has two options: 1) private control plane with private link and customer VPC peering, or 2) full on-prem package. which do you prefer?
03:02 Jared Thompson: private link peering sounds right. we want KMS integration though - keys must be customer-controlled.
03:08 Marcus Lee: ok, we have KMS/HSM integrations. depends on cloud provider — we support AWS KMS, and HSM-backed envelopes if needed. there is a small ops uplift for key rotation and audit. we'll send the KMS integration guide.
03:20 Dr. Anika Patel: and SOC2? our auditors will want the latest report and details about audit logs retention.
03:26 Marcus Lee: yes we can provide SOC 2 type II and an excerpt of audit logs architecture. we also produce per-token audit trails in the Console; retention is configurable for enterprise add-on.
03:36 Sasha Ortiz: any penalties for SLA misses? we have to see uptime guarantees in the amendment.
03:41 Rachel Kim: our Dedicated SLA includes monthly uptime target and credits for certain outages; i'll include the SLA excerpt in the packet. for mission-critical flows we also recommend multi-region fallback which prevents total outage.
03:52 Jared Thompson: what's the expected latency in eu-hosted vs dedicated EU private?
03:57 Marcus Lee: eu-hosted will be comparable to public cloud latencies, typically 30-60ms for 512 token rounds, dedicated private can push lower by choosing smaller batch windows and the low-latency SKU, 20-40ms, depending on model. quantization choices change those numbers too.
04:15 Dr. Anika Patel: can you run a small perf test with our inference suite? we have around 60k requests/day now, growth to 120k. we can share sets of prompts.
04:24 Rachel Kim: yes let's run a 1-week pilot benchmark using your prompts. we'll provision a temporary dedicated pool sized for your peak to mirror production behavior.
04:31 Jared Thompson: provisioning lead time?
04:33 Marcus Lee: for a temporary pool in hosted it can be minutes; dedicated provisioning for a reserved pool varies but for EU we generally need 3-5 business days if GPUs need allocation, but for a pilot we can do a short-lived dedicated cluster within 48 hours if capacity is available.
04:47 Sasha Ortiz: procurement needs pricing tiers and PO terms to present to finance. net30, cancellation windows, and how overages billed.
04:54 Rachel Kim: i'll send three uplift tiers (20%, 40%, and 60% uplift) with committed discounts and overage rates. overages can be charged at the committed uplift rate or a higher burst rate depending on the commitment.
05:06 Dr. Anika Patel: are there minimum contract terms for dedicated? we were on 12-month currently and would consider 12 or 24.
05:13 Rachel Kim: Dedicated is typically 12-month minimum for reserved capacity. we can propose a 12-month with an option to extend at 12 months with a price review.
05:22 Marcus Lee: quick note on model variants: if you pin a quantized variant for cost control, you may see subtle quality diffs - we recommend running a small eval set to validate. Redwood Optimize can automate those checks during rollouts.
05:36 Jared Thompson: ok. about networking: is there a standardized VPC template? we're on AWS with strict subnet restrictions.
05:42 Marcus Lee: yes we have a VPC onboarding checklist and terraform templates. some customers have internal firewall rules that required specific ports, we'll provide the exact list.
05:52 Dr. Anika Patel: any compliance or data residency caveats for EU?
05:55 Marcus Lee: if you go hosted EU, data at rest is in our EU region. for private VPC we can ensure customer-managed KMS, private link, and a dedicated control plane if required for regulatory reasons. we'll include residency mapping in the security pack.
06:08 Sasha Ortiz: procurement question — are discounts front-loaded for the first quarter or spread evenly? finance wants to know cashflow impact.
06:14 Rachel Kim: we can structure discounts either as an upfront credit or as a monthly reduced rate; will propose both ways in the worksheet.
06:20 Jared Thompson: one more technical - how do you handle fallback in case EU capacity is constrained? automatic routing to US?
06:27 Marcus Lee: yes we support smart routing policies; you can prefer EU but allow fallback to US with rate limits. we also support canary rollouts per route.
06:36 Dr. Anika Patel: good. timeline recap?
06:38 Rachel Kim: sure. goal: sign amendment by 2026-12-17 so provisioning can start the week of 2026-12-20 for baseline uplift in january. pilot perf benchmark scheduled target week of 2026-12-10. VPC onboarding planning starts feb, completion by end of march.
06:56 Sasha Ortiz: we can aim for the 17th if pricing and contract terms are clear. procurement needs the pricing worksheet by monday 12/7.
07:04 Rachel Kim: perfect. i'll send that monday. Marcus will send the security pack and KMS guide before then.
07:09 Jared Thompson: what about audit logs retention costs? we want 2 years retention for certain apps.
07:14 Marcus Lee: retention beyond default window is an enterprise add-on; we'll include cost estimates in the security pack.
07:20 Dr. Anika Patel: also want a statement about data deletion/retention for research datasets — legal might ask.
07:26 Rachel Kim: noted, Marcus will include deletion controls and retention toggles in the docs.
07:30 Sasha Ortiz: vendor comparison — we ran a quick eval against ApertureCloud and VoxelServe; ApertureCloud's price was lower but they lacked KMS customer-owned keys. VoxelServe had shorter lead times. why choose Redwood?
07:44 Marcus Lee: from an infra perspective, we emphasize predictable economics, strong observability (token-level cost breakdown), and the progressive VPC/onprem path you asked for. also we automate model rollouts and quality regressions which matter for your close-loop research pipelines.
07:58 Rachel Kim: and the team will partner on the pilot — we don't just hand over API keys.
08:02 Dr. Anika Patel: ok thanks. any remaining blockers?
08:05 Jared Thompson: only that we need the network diagram and exact port list to start internal change requests.
08:10 Marcus Lee: I'll share that today in the VPC package.
08:12 Rachel Kim: and i'll follow up with pricing + amendment.
08:15 Sasha Ortiz: also request a simple SLA snippet we can hand to legal.
08:19 Rachel Kim: will include.
08:21 Rachel Kim: wrap up — next steps recap: Rachel sends pricing and amendment + PO template by 2026-12-07; Marcus sends security pack, SOC2, KMS guide, and VPC network terraform + diagram by 2026-12-06; Luminar provides traffic profile and preferred pilot prompts by 2026-12-08; schedule pilot week of 2026-12-10.
08:39 Dr. Anika Patel: sounds good, thanks everyone.
08:42 Rachel Kim: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to the shared artifacts.
08:46 Meeting end.
